jobs.title: Goodbye to the dog
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 20, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; CHLOE — aged 20, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. CHLOE wears powell's city of books tee. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Thursday. Chloe says goodbye to the dog first. On the porch. She does it properly, on her knees. Wood watches from the bottom step and the strip gives him nothing to say. Panel 1: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young woman kneeling on a porch's top step holding a small dog's face close to hers in rain, a young man sitting on the bottom step (in this panel: CHLOE, BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, close-up of a young woman's forehead pressed to a small dog's forehead (in this panel: CHLOE, BARNABY (the dog)). Chloe says "You. You I'll miss without any complications.". Panel 3: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young man on a porch step looking at a rainy street with an empty speech balloon above him (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "". Panel 4: brush-pen over blue pencil, harsh xerox grain, stark black spotting, rain in frantic vertical hatching, a young woman standing on a porch looking at the back of a seated young man's head while a small dog goes down the steps to him (in this panel: CHLOE, BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). Chloe says "I'll do you Saturday. If you come.". Wood says "I won't.". Chloe says "I know.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby.
